fullText:
If you want to learn how to build self-improving harnesses, check out this paper.

They present Exo, an agent runtime architecture for in-harness learning and adaptation during ongoing work.

Harness optimization usually runs offline, so it needs a representative dataset and many expensive runs before the agent improves.

Exo moves that loop into normal task execution.

The agent edits its own harness code while it works. A small protected layer keeps the execution history and controls which policy version is active, so every change can be inspected.

On AppWorld and SREGym, Exo cuts held-out model cost by 35 to 61% against the same starting policy without self-editing, with comparable correctness. Mean AppWorld task time drops 13%, and median SREGym diagnosis time drops 35%.

fullText:
Weight memory vs. retrieval in agents. Brilliant work from Amazon.

This work shows weight memory can outperform text memory on recall of user facts.

But the best part is that you can leverage both.

Using the same model and user data, this work shows that plain fine-tuning stores user facts in weights at 36.9% accuracy, while on-policy self-distillation reaches 59.9%.

That second number also beats retrieval.

On eight HaluMem-Long users, the distilled model answers with no retrieved context and beats MemOS-style retrieval (47.8%), extracted context (51.9%), and the raw dialogue (51.3%). The gain holds for every user and at 4B, 9B, and 27B.

How it works: a teacher, which is the same model reading the user's memory, trains a student that has to answer without it.

Weight memory has clear limits. It forgets older facts and cannot tell when something was never recorded. A verify-then-regenerate router checks each answer against the text store and adds 6.2 points.

The recommendation is to keep a text store for recent and missing facts, and move stable user knowledge into weights.

user.description: VP Digital Human Research, Epic Games. Emeritus Director, Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems (@MPI_IS). Opinions are my own.

fullText:
The dogma of the last decade in computer vision is that all classical algorithms should be replaced by neural networks. This has been very productive but, counterintuitively, with the latest frontier models, I find myself sometimes turning back to classical methods.

If you have the training data, the dogma still holds. But there are situations where data is hard to get, there exist good classical algorithms for solving a problem, optimization methods are just better, or where some simple code just does the thing you want.

When writing code was time consuming and error prone, training everything made sense. Now, that a frontier model can code up and test solutions quickly, getting a solution through coding can be faster than gathering training data and training a model. Consequently, I think there will be more hybrid approaches that blend trained models and code.

We now have generic, high-level, planners that can execute sequences of lower-level tasks to solve large problems. These lower-level tasks may be solved by a neural network, a classical method, or specialized code written on the fly.

It never pays to be religious about technology. The future is probably hybrid. Pick the thing that works for you.

fullText:
你想让AI自动筛选出美食网站上所有“健康食品”的照片，有时候AI搞不准，这是因为你也没把标准搞清晰

比如你告诉AI，找出所有健康食品

AI开始分类，边界清晰的容易判断，但有些东西未必有唯一正确答案，你也没说清楚所谓的“健康”究竟是指什么

于是你不得不一遍一遍改提示词

谷歌开源了一个AI分类框架：Agile Deliberation，让AI主动寻找那些难以判断的边界案例，反过来帮助人们把模糊的判断标准变成明确可执行的分类规则

简单说，就是AI的角色变了

过去你告诉AI什么是对的，现在AI帮你发现，你自己究竟认为什么是对的

等你的标准越来越清楚，AI再据此优化分类规则

整个流程有两个核心阶段：
Concept Scoping，界定概念范围
先把模糊概念拆开，明确应该包含哪些情况，排除哪些情况，建立初步分类规则

Concept Iteration，迭代分类标准
AI主动去找容易产生争议的边界图片，让用户判断是否符合当前分类标准

然后系统根据反馈不断调整分类指令，再去找新的边界案例，直到规则逐渐符合用户真正想表达的标准

这个框架有几个非常应景的场景

平台内容审核，比如说什么样的广告属于误导性宣传？让AI找出有争议的案例，审核人员判断，完善审核规则

另外一个，企业数据标注，比如什么样的商品照片算高质量，什么样的广告素材符合品牌风格，AI可以通过边界案例帮助建立更一致的判断标准
